stem: A cooperative 6-year-old has a small rubber earplug tip visible in the external ear canal; which office technique is best for removal under direct vision?

options.text: Use a right-angle hook or wax loop/curette to get behind the object, then pull it forward
Push the object further medially until it sits deeper in the canal
Repeatedly compress the tragus to force the object outward
Insert cotton buds around the object and twist
Apply a soothing dressing and review later

explanation: Right-angle hook or wax loop/curette removal is the best technique. This is because the instrument is used to get behind the visible foreign body and then draw it forward under direct vision.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the hook or curette is placed behind the object so it can be brought out forwards under direct vision.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the object should not be pushed deeper into the ear canal.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because tragal compression is not the described technique for direct-vision foreign body removal.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because cotton buds are not appropriate for this removal method and may worsen impaction.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because observation or a dressing does not remove the foreign body from the canal.
